title: id-churn-sentinel per-jurisdiction watch receipt
description: status-us-xx.json, published beside feed-us-xx.xml for EVERY jurisdiction in the registry on every publish, whether or not anything has ever run. It answers the question an empty feed cannot: for the last watch run that covered this jurisdiction, what happened to each of its sources. A hash is deliberately absent in 1.0 — the store binds snapshots to sources and not to runs, so no hash can honestly be attributed to a particular run.

schema_version.description: Bump on any breaking change. The contract is closed (additionalProperties: false), so adding even an optional property is a break.

generated_at.description: When this document was written. NOT when the run happened — read `run.started_at` for that. Regenerating the site does not re-watch anything.

jurisdiction.description: The jurisdiction this receipt is scoped to, as the registry spells it (`TX`, `US`).

coverage.description: `covered`: the newest run in the store covered this jurisdiction. `not_in_run`: it did not, and `run` is the last one that did. `never_covered`: no run ever has, including the case where no run has ever happened.

statement.description: One sentence for a person, which may never claim more than the receipt holds.

outcome_vocabulary.description: Every outcome word this document can use, mapped to the sentence it means. Carried IN the document so a consumer meeting an unfamiliar word can read what it stands for instead of assuming it is benign.

run.description: The last run that covered this jurisdiction, or null when none ever has. When it is null every source reads `not_attempted`, because there is no run whose judgement could be reported.

latest_run.description: The newest run in the store whatever its scope, or null. Present so a `not_in_run` receipt can name the run that skipped this jurisdiction, not only the older one that did not.

counts.description: One key per outcome word, ALWAYS, including the words that did not occur. Omitting zeroes would make a reader reconstruct the missing keys, and the reconstruction they reach for is the reassuring one.

sources.description: Every source the registry holds in this jurisdiction, in id order.

scope.description: What the run declared it covered: a jurisdiction, or `all jurisdictions`.

completed_at.description: null while a run has recorded no terminal outcome. Not the same as a run that failed.

verification_status.description: Whether a HUMAN has confirmed this URL is the page the entry claims it is. Carried here for the same reason it is carried everywhere else: a receipt saying `we read this page and it had not changed` is exactly where a reader is most likely to take the URL as authoritative.

eligible_in_run.description: The RUN's eligibility judgement, not today's. null when the run held no row for this source at all.

eligibility_reasons.description: The reasons the run recorded with that judgement. Empty when the run held no row.

outcome.description: What the last covering run did to this source. Exactly one of nine, and eight of the nine mean the page was NOT compared against its baseline. `not_in_run` and `not_attempted` are separate because `the run never saw this source` and `the run saw it and did not fetch it` lead a reader to different actions.

outcome_statement.description: The sentence `outcome` stands for, repeated per source so a row is readable on its own.
